title: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) - n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz 5G NR) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) filter targeting n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz 5G NR) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on ScAlN on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 3650.3 MHz and bandwidth of 381.9 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz 5G NR)
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: ScAlN on Si
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: PathWave EM Design
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design targeting n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz 5G NR). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3650.3 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       381.9 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.1 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 17.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 32.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 38.0 dB
Q Factor:               10341
Temperature Coefficient:-19.2 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.9 x 2.1 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   10
Electrode Material:     Mo/Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open PathWave EM Design and load the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: ScAlN on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3650.3 MHz, BW 381.9 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.1 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, ScAlN on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N9041B UXA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 10951 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.1 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 17.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 573 MHz offset >= 32.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 6 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 8.8 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +34 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 98%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-04-26
Devices Tested:         34
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.78 dB
Return Loss (meas):     19.4 dB
Rejection (meas):       34.7 dB
Isolation (meas):       43.5 dB
Q Factor (meas):        10341
Group Delay Variation:  7.5 ns
Power Handling:         +33 dBm
Die Yield:              97.3%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated acceptable performance for n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz 5G NR).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Batch-to-batch reproducibility confirmed over 3 wafer lots.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
